To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) website quality influences consumers' perceptions of product quality; (2) website quality has a greater effect on perceived product quality for consumers with higher product information asymmeters; (3) signal credibility strengthens the relationship between website and perceived product quality; (4) cognitive lock-in is a predictor of consumers' repurchase intentions; (5) personalized product recommendations (PPRs) can influence consumers' repurchase intention; and (6) PPRs can influence consumers' store loyalty.
